title: Bathroom drawings, quantities and inspection
intro: Assemble the project drawings, quantities, approval sequence and inspection records, distinguishing a teaching takeoff from purchasing and execution approval.
goals: Tie the sequence to inspections and handover

sections.title: Unify the coordinated project package
sections.text: Index plans, elevations, sections, interfaces and product/material/quantity schedules. Give items identifiers, sources, revisions and approval statuses, reconciling them across documents. Identify work outside the furniture scope and its owner. Completeness means consistent, actionable inputs rather than a large page count.
sections.caption: Consistent IDs, revisions and ownership make the package usable.

sections.title: Separate takeoff from purchasing
sections.text: Exercise only: a rectangular floor measures 2 m by 3 m with no deductions, so 2 × 3 = 6 m². This is a geometric takeoff, not a recommended bathroom size or final order. Purchasing also reviews product layout, cuts, pack sizes and an approved allowance. Link cost to unit rate, source and date; keep net area separate from additions.
sections.caption: 6 m² net under the assumption; purchasing is a separate review.

sections.title: Tie the sequence to inspections and handover
sections.text: Link confirmed products and specialist coordination to approved stages and required pre-concealment inspections, then close/finish according to the selected system. Do not impose one layer sequence on all products. Assign an owner and acceptance evidence to each hold point, followed by defects, reinspection, as-built information and operation/maintenance records. Keep outstanding items visible at handover.
sections.caption: Required evidence controls release of the next stage.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: The 6 m² teaching takeoff is entered directly as a purchase order before packs and cutting layout are reviewed. Retain 6 m² as net takeoff and hold the order quantity and cost until product selection, layout and a dated quotation are resolved.
example.decision: Decision: keep takeoff and order quantity separate.

quiz.question: Exercise floor 2 m × 3 m, no deductions: net area?
quiz.explanation: Length times width gives 6 m² of area, not volume or an order quantity.

assignment.prompt: Submit a package index, teaching takeoff, purchase inputs and a stage/inspection/handover plan.

faq.question: Does correct area arithmetic release purchasing?
faq.answer: No. Review product, layout, pack sizes, approved allowances and dated quotation.
